arml-local-2010-theme-01.prompt: The Vancouver Olympic Committee decides to build a conical mountain of snow with a base radius of $8$ kilometers. Because they run out of snow on the way up, they instead shape the mountain into the frustum of a cone $4$ kilometers high, with the top of the frustum having radius $5$ kilometers (and the bottom radius $8$ kilometers, as in the picture). Compute the *exposed* surface area (in sq km) of the resulting snow \"mountain\" (the top and the slanted side).

arml-local-2010-theme-02.prompt:
The cross section of a torch pillar is an obtuse triangle $\triangle ABC$ with base $AB$ $5$ meters long and height $15$ meters. $D$ is the foot of the altitude from $C$ to line $AB$, and $AD$ is also $5$ meters long ($A$ lies between $D$ and $B$). The pillar is supported internally by beams with a square cross section, stacked as in the picture. The first supporting beam $S_1$ has one side on $AB$ and has one corner on $AC$ and the opposite corner on $BC$. The second beam $S_2$ is placed on top of $S_1$ and also has one corner on $AC$ and the opposite corner on $BC$. This process is repeated forever: beam $S_{n+1}$ is placed on top of beam $S_n$, and each beam has one corner on $AC$ and the opposite corner on $BC$.

Compute (in meters) the side length of $S_1$.

arml-local-2010-theme-05.prompt:
The cross section of a torch pillar is a right triangle $\triangle ABC$ with base $AB$ $3$ meters long and height $AC$ $4$ meters (right angle at $A$). The pillar is supported internally by beams with a circular cross section. The first beam $C_1$ is tangent to $AB$, $AC$, and $BC$. The second circular beam $C_2$ is placed on top of the first: it is tangent to $AC$ and $BC$, and externally tangent to $C_1$. (The centers of both circles lie on the bisector of $\angle ACB$.)

Compute (in meters) the radius of $C_1$.

arml-local-2010-theme-07.prompt: The Finnish hockey team wishes to practice playing 5-on-5, but has 11 players. They use the following substitution system: the players are numbered $1$ to $11$. For the first three minutes, players $2$-$6$ play against players $7$-$11$, with player $1$ sitting out. Then player $1$ replaces player $2$ and that group plays for three minutes. In general, player $n$ replaces player $n+1$ after three minutes (except for player $11$, who replaces player $1$). The practice continues until players $2$-$6$ are going to play $7$-$11$, and the practice stops (before $2$-$6$ and $7$-$11$ play again). Compute the length (in minutes) of the practice.

Teams are ranked by total match points; teams with the same number of match points are ranked in decreasing order by goal difference (goals scored by the team minus goals scored against it, which may be negative).

The United States, Finland, Canada, and Russia are playing in a round-robin hockey tournament. The incomplete chart below reports some of the results from matches that have already been played. One team defeated another by a score of $5$-$1$, and no other team has scored as many as five goals in one match. Also, one team won one of its matches by one more goal than it won another game. With this information, complete the chart (all cells).

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| US |  | 2 |  | 1 |  | 0 |  |
| Canada |  |  |  | 0 |  |  |  |
| Russia | 2 |  |  |  | 2 |  | 2 |
| Finland | 3 |  |  |  |  | 11 | 1 |
